clues: A chemist was designing synthetic sugar derivatives to help manage diabetes when he discovered this drug in 1979. It did not treat diabetes well, but shared similarities with acetazolamide, which led to its first clinical indication

Because it inhibits carbonic anhydrase, patients might report that carbonated beverages taste flat or metallic. Other side effects might include weight loss, cognitive slowing, and word finding difficulties.
Because of these cognitive side effects, this anti-epileptic is sometimes known by the nickname 'dopamax'
Before the 1920s, this disease was uniformly fatal. In 1926, scientists discovered that eating a half-pound of raw liver daily cured the disease which led to a 1934 Nobel Prize

Patients of European ancestry who were affected by this autoimmune disease were historically described as having a waxy, lemon-yellow appearance. Because of the associated neurological symptoms such as hallucinations and paranoia, some patients were mis-diagnosed as having a psychiatric disorder

Dr. William Castle was the first to describe the relationship between the food (extrinsic) factor and an intrinsic factor of normal gastric juice. We now know that this disease is caused by antibodies against intrinsic factor.

In 'The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn', Huck's father suffers from this condition. If that's not helpful, Nicolas Cage also played a character who suffered from this in the 1995 film, Leaving Las Vegas. His performance won him the Academy Award for Best Actor in 1996

For centuries, this was misidentified as 'phrenitis' or an inflammation of the brain. It was formally identified and named in 1813, which marked a turning point in the clinical recognition of this as a disease that could be managed medically
Patients might develop confusion, shaking, and vivid hallucinations which popularized an older idiom 'seeing pink elephants'

The organism causing this disease is suspected to have evolved in the Mesozoic era prior to the breakup of the supercontinent Pangaea. It has plagued humanity since antiquity, with pre-Incan pottery depicting facial disfigurements and lesions caused by the disease

During the massive global push to eradicate malaria in the 1950s, the World Health Organization sprayed widespread amounts of DDT, which inadvertently wiped out some species that transmit the visceral version of this disease

Currently, cutaneous versions are the most common presentation transmitted via the bites of infected female sandflies. Although this disease is found in 98 countries, 90% of new cases occur in just 13 countries.
